summary: SSE session aborts mid-response when inference latency spikes under burst load
description:
Issue summary: BrightLens reports that streaming chat responses (SSE) frequently abort mid-token during sustained traffic bursts. The client receives an abrupt end-of-stream after 3–10s of no tokens, even though the inference job eventually completes on the backend.

Impact: Several BrightLens customers see truncated assistant replies inside the product. User sessions are not recoverable without a full request retry. This affects multiple customer endpoints and is causing ongoing support escalations.

Environment: prod cluster servicing BrightLens (dedicated pool) in us-east-1. Autoscaling group of 8 A100 GPUs with dedicated serving-runtime instances behind an Envoy API gateway and AWS ALB. Model pins: redwood-vicuna-13B (quantized) for assistant endpoints.

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer and reproduced by Support):
1) Start a chat session with a 2k token context that triggers long-form generation.
2) Fire a burst of concurrent streaming requests (10–15) from separate client machines.
3) Observe one or more streaming connections close with no closing token or error body; client sees connection close or SSE malformed event.

Observed behavior: The SSE connection terminates abruptly during generation. Server-side logs show the inference worker continuing to generate and finish the output 5–15s after the client observed the abort. No explicit 5xx logged at the app layer for the aborted connection. Envoy metrics show increased upstream timeouts and connection resets around the same timestamps.

Relevant logs & excerpts:
- Envoy upstream log snippets: "upstream reset: connection_failure" and repeated "upstream headers timeout" entries around 2026-03-11T18:22:xxZ.
- ALB access log example: "request_processing_time=0.05 target_processing_time=12.34 response_processing_time=0.00 elb_status_code=504 target_status_code=502"
- Serving-runtime worker log (inferred): "[2026-03-11T18:22:12Z] generate_stream: started request id=abc123" then "[2026-03-11T18:22:24Z] generate_stream: finished request id=abc123 duration=12.0s" with no associated error.
- Client telemetry: SSE event stream closed with WebSocket/HTTP client code 1006 / ECONNRESET in customer traces.

Hypothesis / initial investigation notes:
- Load balancer idle or target timeout (ALB/Envoy) is closing connections when backend generation exceeds configured thresholds under bursty concurrency. The serving runtime continues producing tokens but the connection path is torn down by middleboxes.
- There is evidence of Envoy dropping upstream connections when concurrency crosses a threshold causing queueing delays; this manifests as upstream resets in Envoy logs.
- Client heartbeats are not enabled by default for SSE flows, so multi-second gaps between tokens are treated as silent and result in connection closure by intermediaries.

Customer impact workaround provided to BrightLens:
- Short-term: Recommend client implement automatic retry with conversation state on stream close and reduce per-request max_new_tokens to keep generation chunks < 6s.
- Platform workaround: We increased ALB and Envoy idle/timeout thresholds for the BrightLens dedicated pool to 120s and temporarily scaled the serving pool from 8->12 GPUs to reduce queueing.

Next steps already taken:
- Eng oncall (Diego) created INT-4512 to run a reproducer load test and capture pcap/trace.
- Added enhanced Envoy debug logging for the BrightLens target group for 24h.
- Engineering set a short-term config bump on ALB/Envoy timeouts and informed BrightLens.

Proposed longer-term fixes:
- Add periodic SSE keepalive/heartbeat frames from the serving-runtime to prevent intermediaries from treating gaps as idle.
- Improve real-time metrics for token emission latency per-request so autoscaler and routing can detect sustained per-request stalls and redirect to higher-throughput nodes.
- Tune queueing/backpressure behavior in the serving-runtime to prioritize steady token emission under concurrency.

Open questions:
- Is the Envoy idle timeout bump safe across other tenants in the same VPC? (Security/infra to advise).
- Can we add configurable keepalives in the runtime without regressions on memory/CPU?

investigation_notes: Reproducer (INT-4512) shows correlation between concurrent request queue depth and Envoy upstream_resets. Token emission SLO violation occurs when per-request generation >8–10s combined with 10+ concurrent streams. No serving-runtime OOMs or worker crashes observed.
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigations applied: ALB/Envoy timeouts increased and serving pool scaled. Customer instructed to implement retries and smaller generation chunks. Permanent fix planned: runtime keepalive + token-latency metrics work.
root_cause: Middlebox timeouts (Envoy/ALB) closing idle streaming connections during sustained token-generation delays caused by bursty concurrency and queueing in the dedicated serving pool.
resolution: Mitigation in place; engineering backlog item created for runtime keepalive and improved token emission metrics. Monitoring remains active; ticket will be updated with code PRs and rollout plan.
